newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn, soy harvest areas seen dry but colder.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn, soy harvest areas seen dry but colder.

text.p: Key U.S. corn and soybean growing areas in the Midwest are expected to be mostly dry during the next 10 days, aiding harvest progress, but the temperature outlook has turned colder, meteorologists said.

"It looks like harvesting will really be rolling the next 10 days. There is just not much precipitation in the forecast at all for any portion of the corn belt," meteorologist Craig Solberg of Freese-Notis Weather said.
Solberg added, however, that weather maps looked colder with temperatures seen dipping on Thursday and Friday.
He said Thursday morning would see temperatures in the northwest corn belt (northern Iowa, Minnesota and northwest Illinois) dip as low as 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Then on Friday he anticipated lows of 33 to 37 degrees F in northeast Illinois, northern Indiana and northern Ohio and 30 to 32 degrees F in Wisconsin and Michigan.
"Thursday and Friday morning are going to be the coldest of the fall period for those areas," Solberg said.
"A hard freeze where we see temperatures in the 20s (F) at this point does not look to be a real big likelihood. It looks like a frost event, not a freeze event," he added.
Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp, also said the outlook had turned colder.
"It is a stronger high pressure system than originally thought. We may see low temperatures of 30 to 35 degrees (F) by Thursday morning in northern Iowa northward," he said.
He forecast similar lows in Wisconsin and Michigan on either Thursday or Friday morning, with the possibility the cold weather might dip into northern Illinois, northern Indiana and northwest Ohio.
Temperatures would drop in areas such as central Illinois and southern Iowa to around 37 to 40 degrees F, Burgio said.
WSC's Burgio said there would be little rainfall over the next few days.
"We may have a few sprinkles but nothing important," he said.
Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for above to much above normal temperatures and normal to no precipitation in the U.S. Midwest October 6 through 10.

Government reports issued Monday indicated the U.S. corn harvest was nine percent complete as of Sunday, behind the five-year average of 17 percent. The soybean harvest was four percent done, behind an average of 15 percent.
